extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: You MUST import and use BOTH audioManager AND speechManager. Import speechManager from '../../../lib/sim-engine/speech'. Use audioManager.play() for sound effects (valid: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint). Use speechManager.speak() for spoken teaching slide narration, challenge questions, correct/incorrect feedback, and hints. The game must teach: (1) Percentage — percent means 'per hundred'. 25% means 25 out of 100. The symbol % means /100. (2) Fraction-Decimal-Percentage relationship — 1/4 = 0.25 = 25%. 1/2 = 0.5 = 50%. 3/4 = 0.75 = 75%. 1/5 = 0.2 = 20%. To convert fraction to percentage: multiply by 100. 1/4 x 100 = 25%. To convert percentage to fraction: write as /100 and simplify. 25% = 25/100 = 1/4. (3) Decimal to percentage: multiply by 100 (move decimal right 2 places). 0.45 x 100 = 45%. Percentage to decimal: divide by 100 (move decimal left 2 places). 45% = 0.45. (4) Pictorial representation — 100-grid showing shaded portions. 25% = 25 squares shaded out of 100. (5) Word problems — 'x% of N' means (x/100) x N. 20% of 50 = (20/100) x 50 = 10. 60% of 40 students = (60/100) x 40 = 24 girls. (6) Data handling — pictograph uses pictures to represent data. Bar graph uses bars of different heights. Line graph shows trends over time. Pie chart shows parts of a whole as sectors. (7) Patterns — unit of repeat: ABABAB (repeat AB). Progressive: 2, 4, 6, 8 (add 2 each time). 3, 6, 12, 24 (multiply by 2). Multi-characteristic: alternating color and shape while growing. Triangular numbers: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15 (add 2, add 3, add 4, add 5). Square numbers: 1, 4, 9, 16, 25 (1x1, 2x2, 3x3, 4x4, 5x5). Misconceptions: 'percent means out of 10' (WRONG — percent means out of 100), '0.5 = 5%' (WRONG — 0.5 x 100 = 50%, not 5%), '25% of 40 is 25 x 40 = 1000' (WRONG — 25% of 40 means 25/100 x 40 = 10, not 25 times 40), 'triangular numbers are the same as square numbers' (WRONG — triangular: 1,3,6,10,15 (adding increasing amounts); square: 1,4,9,16,25 (n times n)), 'a progressive pattern always adds' (WRONG — progressive patterns can also multiply, like 2, 4, 8, 16).
